payload.claim: The witness for criterion 2 (`test_a_stack_order_admits_a_spec_whose_dependencies_are_in_it_or_on_the_default_branch`) sets up TE-21 as 'MERGED at a stale spec_sha' to prove that stack mode credits a dependency merged at *any* spec_sha, not just the current one — the spec's own notes list 'reading MERGED only at the current spec_sha' as a case this witness must fail. But TE-21 has no `depends_on` of its own, so it is never removed from the ordinary candidate pool (its stale-sha row does not match its current spec_sha, so the DONE_STATES filter at scheduler.py:865 does not exclude it) and `_stack_order` takes it as a trivially-ready, stand-alone candidate regardless of whether `merged_anywhere` credits it. So TE-31 (which depends on TE-21) is admitted even if the 'any spec_sha' merge credit is broken, and this sub-case adds no real coverage beyond what TE-32 (retired) and TE-33 (landed push) already provide in the same test. The mechanism happens to stay covered overall only through the pre-existing, non-stack test `test_a_merged_parent_satisfies_whatever_sha_it_ran_at` (line 1441), not through this new witness.
